title: Gemini 4 Argon
summary: Argon, a tool employed by the Chrome team, was instrumental in re-architecting Chromium's massive codebase. It helped separate core webpage handling from a ~6 million-line legacy folder within the 40 million-line Chromium project. By enabling multiple clean code changes simultaneously, Argon accelerated an extensive architectural refactor across hundreds of files, completing work that would have taken months in a matter of weeks. This foundational change will benefit Chrome's billions of users by allowing live webpages to move fluidly between tabs, side panels, and floating windows without reloading, thereby eliminating an entire category of browser crashes and significantly improving user experience.

title: Firefox Enterprise
summary: Firefox Enterprise emphasizes "Sovereignty," empowering organizations to take full control over their browser deployment and data. This is achieved by enabling on-premises installation of Firefox Enterprise within a company's own infrastructure. This capability allows businesses to define and audit where their data, policies, and management reside, ensuring complete oversight and control over these critical elements.

title: Apple HomeView
summary:
The Apple HomeView, available November 13 for pre-order, is a new smart display designed to keep homes connected, entertained, and informed, prioritizing privacy for all users.

Powered by Apple Intelligence, Siri AI offers a personalized assistant experience, understanding individual contexts, accessing broad world knowledge, and engaging in seamless conversations, all while protecting privacy through Private Cloud Compute and Secure Exclaves. The device recognizes up to six users, delivering a customized experience for each, keeping personal content separate and secure.

HomeView features a vibrant 7-inch Liquid Retina display with True Tone and adaptive brightness, alongside powerful speakers delivering Spatial Audio and beamforming microphones for clear sound. Its 12MP Center Stage camera ensures participants remain centered during video calls. It serves as an ultimate smart home dashboard, integrating with the Home app for controlling accessories, monitoring cameras, and receiving alerts like smoke/CO detector sounds.

Designed with an adjustable domed aluminum base (available in Silver, Starlight, Rose Pink, Space Gray), a wall-mounted option is also offered. Customizable faces allow users to display photos, calendars, or interactive artwork. HomeView supports various Apple and third-party apps, and features like Handoff for seamless content transitions. Apple emphasizes robust privacy protections, ensuring user data is processed securely and remains separate. Guided shopping, installation services, and personal setup are available to assist customers.

title: Iosevka is an open-source, sans-serif and slab-serif monospace font
summary: Iosevka is an open-source, sans-serif, and slab-serif monospace font. By default, its glyphs are slender, measuring exactly 1/2em wide, which allows users to fit more columns on a screen compared to other fonts. The font is available in two widths: Normal and an Extended version, with the latter providing more space between characters for those who prefer it.

chinese_summary: Iosevka 是一款开源的无衬线和粗衬线等宽字体。默认情况下，其字形纤细，宽度恰好为 1/2em，相比其他字体，这使得用户能够在屏幕上容纳更多列。该字体提供两种宽度版本：常规版和扩展版，后者为偏好更大字符间距的用户提供了更多空间。

title: Amazon pushes up prices across the Internet
summary:
The article argues that Amazon's business model systematically inflates prices across the entire internet, a central claim in the US Federal Trade Commission's upcoming antitrust case against the company. Amazon charges third-party sellers a multitude of fees, which can consume nearly half of a sale, up from 19% in 2014. While a basic commission is comparable to competitors, other fees for fulfillment (required for Prime eligibility) and advertising are virtually mandatory for sellers to achieve visibility and sales on the platform.

These high operational costs compel sellers to raise their product prices. Crucially, Amazon's "Fair Pricing Policy" prohibits sellers from offering their items cheaper elsewhere, including their own websites. Violating this policy can lead to the removal of the "Add to Cart" button or even seller suspension. As a result, sellers are forced to maintain their Amazon-inflated prices across all platforms, ensuring consumers pay "Amazon prices" even when not shopping on Amazon.

Despite the frustration, sellers often cannot abandon Amazon due to its dominance, accounting for about 40% of US online retail sales. Regulators have noticed, with the FTC and 17 US states suing Amazon for illegally maintaining its monopoly and punishing sellers who offer lower prices elsewhere. Germany has also ordered Amazon to cease controlling seller prices. The author highlights that Amazon's extensive reach means its pricing structure impacts the broader online retail landscape, regardless of where consumers shop.
chinese_title: Amazon pushes up prices across the Internet
chinese_summary:
文章指出，亚马逊的商业模式系统性地推高了整个互联网上的价格，这是美国联邦贸易委员会（FTC）即将对该公司提起的反垄断诉讼中的核心主张。亚马逊向第三方卖家收取各种费用，这些费用可能吞噬近一半的销售额，远高于2014年的19%。虽然基本佣金与竞争对手相当，但用于履约服务（Prime会员资格的强制要求）和广告的其他费用，对卖家在平台上获得曝光和销量来说，实际上是强制性的。

这些高昂的运营成本迫使卖家提高产品价格。更重要的是，亚马逊的“公平定价政策”禁止卖家在其他地方（包括他们自己的网站）以更低的价格销售商品。违反此政策可能导致“加入购物车”按钮被移除，甚至卖家账户被暂停。结果，卖家被迫在所有平台上维持其被亚马逊抬高后的价格，确保消费者即使不在亚马逊购物，也要支付“亚马逊价格”。

尽管如此令人沮丧，由于亚马逊的主导地位（占据美国在线零售销售额的约40%），卖家往往无法放弃它。监管机构已有所察觉，FTC和美国17个州正在起诉亚马逊非法维持其垄断地位，并惩罚在其他地方提供更低价格的卖家。德国也已命令亚马逊停止控制卖家价格。作者强调，亚马逊广泛的触角意味着其定价结构影响着更广阔的在线零售格局，无论消费者在哪里购物。

title: OpenAI engineer arrested in bugging of executive conference room
summary:
OpenAI engineer Abdulrahman Alfozan, 35, a Saudi national, has been arrested and charged with hiding an audio recording device in an executive conference room at the company's San Francisco headquarters. The device, a thumb-sized Seeed XIAO ESP32-S3 Sense, was discovered September 30, concealed in toilet paper and plugged into a television's USB port. Prosecutors allege it was installed around September 28.

Alfozan, who joined OpenAI in July 2025, was not authorized to enter the room, which frequently held discussions about confidential technical, commercial, and strategic information. Surveillance footage placed him near the room, and he had used a productivity tool to inquire about building addresses and meeting locations. A chatbot account linked to his spouse also made queries about building, obscuring, and accessing recording devices, including the specific model found.

Additionally, a second, similar recording device was found in an unattended bag belonging to Alfozan. U.S. Attorney Craig Missakian labeled the incident a "matter of national security," with the FBI emphasizing the protection of U.S. AI innovation as a top counterintelligence priority.

OpenAI discovered the device during a security sweep, utilized its AI models to identify it, and promptly informed the FBI. The company coordinated Alfozan's termination with investigators and stated there is no indication he accessed sensitive data like model weights or source code. If convicted, Alfozan faces up to five years in prison. OpenAI also believes he intended to place more devices in sensitive areas.
